column4: who ends it: an owned helper, a PR 699 spawn table row, or why it is off the hook, guard, CI and doctor paths
The owned-group helper itself: `GroupOwner::prepare` runs first, and every path signals the group before it reaps the leader.
The bounded reader `rq` itself: an owned group with a deadline capped at the outer one (spawn table rows 1 to 22a, 24 to 33, 42, 43).
The guard config reader `gc` itself: an owned group with a 3 s deadline (spawn table rows 27 to 29).

The stdin-feeding spawn helper; its caller owns the child: `owned_output`, `rq` and doctor's `run_captured_with` prepare an owned group first, and ci's `git_with_stdin` runs in ci's group (spawn table row 34, G(ci)).
Doctor's bounded runner, after `GroupOwner::prepare` (spawn table row 41, O).
Windows only: `taskkill /T /F` on a timed-out doctor child, started without waiting so it cannot extend the deadline (spawn table row 41; Windows has no group design).
Doctor's foreground probes, kept in the operator's job on purpose because they may prompt on the terminal (spawn table row 40, G(op)).
The doctor runner probe, after `GroupOwner::prepare`, stdin null (spawn table row 47, O).
Doctor's `config --get core.hooksPath`, which reads no objects (spawn table row 44, G(op)).
`ids::Git::new` without limits: ci's id registry merge rule runs in ci's group (spawn table row 37, G(ci)); doctor's `ids::check` in the operator's job (row 46, G(op)). With limits it runs on `rq`.
The adopter's release script from the pre-push hook, in the hook's own group because it may prompt on the terminal (spawn table row 23, X).
